# Adjudication Task — Chapter 551

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃551화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|여섯 명의 젊은 남녀가 은밀하게 하남을 빠져나가던 그 날 밤. 두 사람은 달빛이 내리쬐는 정자에서 술잔을 부딪쳤다.
  6|
  7|쨍.
  8|
  9|티 없이 맑은 소리와 함께 꺾이는 술잔. 단숨에 술을 입안으로 털어 넣은 화왕(火王) 적천강이 나직이 뇌까렸다.
 10|
 11|“오늘따라 술맛이 별로군.”
 12|
 13|맞은편에 앉아 있던 매종학이 빙긋 웃었다.
 14|
 15|“여아홍(女兒紅)이 입에 맞지 않으신 모양이오.”
 16|
 17|“모르겠소. 아까부터 목이 칼칼하고 혀가 쓴데, 혹시 술에 독이라도 탄 것 아니오?
 18|
 19|다른 사람은 농담 삼아서라도 절대 할 수 없는 말이다.
 20|
 21|그야말로 적천강이기에 가능한 말이었고, 그 상대가 매종학이라 웃고 넘어갈 수 있는 이야기였다.
 22|
 23|“내가 적 대협을 독살하다니. 그럴 리가 있겠소. 다만 나중에 한 번 시도는 해 보리다.”
 24|
 25|“잘 알아보고 쓰시오. 이제는 무형지독(無形至毒)도 견딜 자신이 생겼으니까.”
 26|
 27|“오. 그럼 무림맹의 총력을 기울여서라도 알아보겠소.”
 28|
 29|적천강이 불퉁하게 대꾸했다.
 30|
 31|“겁나는군. 누가 들으면 진심인 줄 알겠소.”
 32|
 33|“아, 농이었소? 난 또.”
 34|
 35|“……?”
 36|
 37|설마?
 38|
 39|이제야 깨달았다는 듯이 고개를 끄덕이는 매종학의 모습에, 적천강은 간담이 서늘해졌다.
 40|
 41|‘이런 정신 나간 늙은이를 봤나.’
 42|
 43|겉모습만 젊어졌을 뿐, 제정신이 아닌 부분에서는 사십여 년 전이나 지금이나 똑같다.
 44|
 45|하긴, 굳이 멀리 갈 필요도 없이 청풍 그놈만 봐도 알 수 있는 사실이었다.
 46|
 47|‘콩 심은 데 콩 난다고, 하여간 스승이나 제자나…….’
 48|
 49|그 순간, 술잔을 채우던 적천강의 손길이 덜컥 흔들렸다.
 50|
 51|‘제자라.’
 52|
 53|촤악. 한가득 흘러넘친 술 위로 씁쓸한 표정을 짓고 있는 어느 중년인의 얼굴이 비친다.
 54|
 55|익숙하면서도 아직은 낯선 자신의 모습을 물끄러미 바라보던 적천강이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 56|
 57|“아무 일도 없겠지. 그렇지 않소?”
 58|
 59|매종학이 자신의 술잔을 채우며 되물었다.
 60|
 61|“걱정되시오?”
 62|
 63|“걱정은 무슨! 사내가 약관이 넘었으면 응당 제 갈 길을 가야지. 일가(一家)를 이루어도 이상하지 않을 나이인데.”
 64|
 65|애써 큰소리를 쳤지만 적천강의 입맛은 여전히 쓰기만 했다. 지금쯤이면 남쪽을 향해 떠나고 있을, 누군가의 얼굴이 생각나서였다.
 66|
 67|그리고 그런 그의 얼굴 위로 얼핏 스쳐 지나간 감정을, 매종학은 놓치지 않았다.
 68|
 69|“멀리 못 갔을 거요.”
 70|
 71|흘리듯 건넨 말에, 적천강이 씁쓸하게 대꾸했다.
 72|
 73|“……이미 인사는 나눴거늘, 다시 마주하면 뭣 하겠소. 발길만 무거울 뿐이지.”
 74|
 75|“듣고 보니 그렇구려.”
 76|
 77|“그래서, 대답은?”
 78|
 79|“음? 뭘 말이오?”
 80|
 81|“이 양반이 맹주가 되더니 귀가 막혔나. 그…… 아까 물어본 것 있지 않소.”
 82|
 83|술잔을 만지작거리던 적천강이 조심스럽게 말을 이었다.
 84|
 85|“아무 일도 없을 거요. 그렇지?”
 86|
 87|잠시 뭔가를 생각하던 매종학이 대답했다.
 88|
 89|“그럴 수도 있고, 아닐 수도 있소.”
 90|
 91|“……그걸 지금 말이라고 하는 거요?”
 92|
 93|“일단 말은 맞소. 지금 막 내 입으로 한 말이니.”
 94|
 95|“염병할. 미치고 환장하겠네. 그런 대답은 누구든 할 수 있는 거 아니오?”
 96|
 97|“어라. 그것도 그렇구려.”
 98|
 99|“그럼 무림 맹주로서 적절한 대답을 찾아보라고. 적절한 대답을!”
100|
101|벌컥 역정을 내는 적천강의 모습에, 매종학이 빙긋 웃었다.
102|
103|“그는 잘 해낼 거요. 지금까지 늘 그래 왔듯이.”
104|
105|“그 말, 진심이오?”
106|
107|“물론. 믿음이 없었다면 왜 화룡각에 그런 막중한 임무를 맡겼겠소.”
108|
109|적천강이 한결 누그러진 목소리로 입을 열었다.
110|
111|“혹, 만약의 상황을 위한 대비책도 마련해 둔 거요?”
112|
113|“은영각의 눈과 귀는 천하 곳곳에 있소. 남만(南蠻)도 예외는 아니지.”
114|
115|“……!”
116|
117|“화룡각을 남만으로 보낸 것은 가장 빠르고 확실한 방법이기 때문이오. 당장 일군(一軍)을 일으키기에는 시일이 촉박하니.”
118|
119|현재 무림맹의 규모는 과거 정마대전 때와 비교해도 결코 작지 않았다. 아니, 오히려 그 이상이라 해도 과언이 아니다.
120|
121|소림사와 사천문을 비롯한 몇몇 문파가 큰 피해를 입긴 했으나, 아직 정파의 영역이라 할 수 있는 구주(九州)에 속한 어느 성도 무너지지 않았으니까.
122|
123|문제는 병력을 소집하고, 남만으로 보내는 데까지 걸리는 시간과 물자였다.
124|
125|그리고 진태경이 이끄는 화룡각이야말로 무림맹이 자신 있게 내밀 수 있는 몇 안 되는 패라고 할 수 있었다.
126|
127|“으음.”
128|
129|하지만 어떤 말을 들어도 적천강의 근심은 사라지지 않았다.
130|
131|말없이 술잔만 노려보는 그에게, 매종학이 개미만 한 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
132|
133|“가장 확실한 지원이 있긴 한데.”
134|
135|“응? 지금 뭐라 했소?”
136|
137|“별것 아니오. 그냥 혼잣말이었소.”
138|
139|“감히 누굴 속이려고! 분명 뭐라 하는 것을 이 귀로 똑똑히 들었거늘!”
140|
141|“고정하시고 마저 술이나 드시오. 그럼 내 생각해 보리다.”
142|
143|매종학을 빤히 응시하던 적천강이 투덜거렸다.
144|
145|“맛도 없는 술을 뭘 자꾸 먹이려고.”
146|
147|“적 대협.”
148|
149|“왜 그러시오.”
150|
151|퉁명스럽게 대꾸하는 적천강을, 매종학이 그윽한 눈빛으로 응시했다.
152|
153|“그 맛 없는 술을, 이미 다섯 동이나 드셨소.”
154|
155|“…….”
156|
157|“지금 마시고 있는 게 여섯 동이째요.”
158|
159|“…….”
160|
161|“우선 마십시다.”
162|
163|조용히 입을 다문 적천강이 술잔을 기울였다.
164|
165|향긋한 주향과 함께 목을 타고 넘어가는 술이, 말했던 것만큼 쓰지 않았다. 술잔과 함께 뒤로 젖혀진 그의 얼굴에 은은한 달빛이 닿았다.
166|
167|‘저 아래쯤 어디에 있으려나.’
168|
169|무정한 놈. 그래도 떠나기 전 얼굴 한 번 정도는 비춰 주지.
170|
171|마음속에서 들려온 중얼거림은, 이내 어디선가 불어온 함께 흩어졌다.
172|
173|
174|
175|* * *
176|
177|
178|
179|다그닥. 다그닥.
180|
181|나이든 말의 발걸음은 느렸고, 전신을 빈틈없이 감싼 볏짚은 차갑고 따가웠다.
182|
183|마차 밖에서는 호객하는 장사치들과 사람들의 목소리가 천천히 멀어지고 있었다.
184|
185|‘빠져나왔나?’
186|
187|그런 생각이 뇌리에 떠오른 순간. 누군가의 속삭임이 귓가를 파고들었다.
188|
189|“조장님. 똥 마려워요.”
190|
191|“…….”
192|
193|혁무진 이 미친놈은 여기서까지 염병하고 자빠졌네.
194|
195|지금은 최대한 움직임을 줄여야 하기에 무력 진압도 불가능한 상황. 나는 한껏 목소리를 죽여 윽박질렀다.
196|
197|“미친놈아. 내가 미리 싸랬지.”
198|
199|“긴장해서 그래요. 긴장해서.”
200|
201|“그럼 참아, 시벌 놈아.”
202|
203|“왜 욕을 하고 그러세요? 무슨 말을 못 하겠네.”
204|
205|“욕이 안 나오게 생겼냐, 지금? 여기서 싸면 냄새는 어쩔래?”
206|
207|이불 덮고 방귀만 뀌어도 욕이 나오는데, 함께 볏짚에 파묻혀 있는 상황에서 그런 불상사가 벌어지는 건 죽어도 거부하고 싶다.
208|
209|“안 그래도 제가 생각을 해 봤는데요. 차라리 그냥 싸 버리면 냄새가 나서 검문도 쉽게 통과하지 않을까요?”
210|
211|“죽어. 제발 죽어.”
212|
213|“죄송합니다. 참을 만큼 참았는데 안 될 것 같아요. 전 여기까지인가 봐요.”
214|
215|“야, 무진아. 잠깐만. 잠깐만 기다려 봐.”
216|
217|“죄는 나중에 달게 받겠습니다.”
218|
219|안 돼! 개새끼야!
220|
221|공포에 질린 내가 위장이고 나발이고 벌떡 일어나려던 그 순간이었다.
222|
223|“낙양(洛陽)의 중심거리를 지났어요. 인적도 없는 산길이니 잠깐 나오셔도 좋아요.”
224|
225|“허억!”
226|
227|“푸하!”
228|
229|파사삭!
230|
231|볏짚을 뚫고 튀어나온 혁무진이 풀숲을 향해 냅다 뛰어간다. 벼랑 끝에서 목숨을 건진 나는 구원자를 향해 연거푸 고개를 숙였다.
232|
233|“감사합니다. 착하게 살겠습니다. 정말 감사합니다.”
234|
235|“검문에 시간이 걸려서 그런지, 혁 소협이 많이 급했나 보네요. 늦지 않아서 다행이에요.”
236|
237|익숙한 목소리. 그러나 싱긋 웃는 여인의 얼굴은 낯설었다.
238|
239|높게 솟은 나뭇가지 사이로 쏟아지는 달빛 아래, 양 볼에 가득한 주근깨와 푸석푸석한 피부가 유난히 눈에 띄었다.
240|
241|‘봐도 봐도 신기하네.’
242|
243|이목구비와 사소한 부분이 바뀌었을 뿐인데, 그것만으로도 인상이 확 달라지다니.
244|
245|내 시선을 눈치챈 여인, 주화란이 자신의 얼굴을 매만졌다.
246|
247|“아, 제가 조금 변하긴 했죠?”
248|
249|“네. 그래도 눈은 여전한데요?”
250|
251|아름다운 검푸른 눈동자에 웃음이 스쳤다.
252|
253|“그건 면구(面具)로 어떻게 할 수 있는 부분이 아니라서요. 그나마 송 당주가 아니었다면 당장 이 정도의 면구를 구하기 힘들었을 거예요.”
254|
255|마부석에 앉아 있던 송일섬이 덤덤하게 덧붙였다.
256|
257|“별것 아니오. 살려고 익힌 잡기(雜器) 정도지.”
258|
259|“잡기치고는 훌륭한데?”
260|
261|“어차피 빈말이겠지만, 우선 칭찬은 고맙다고 해 두지.”
262|
263|저놈도 어지간히 삐딱한 놈이다. 진심이었는데.
264|
265|완전 다른 사람이 된 주화란의 얼굴은 송일섬의 솜씨였다.
266|
267|일찍이 밑바닥부터 산전수전 겪으며 살아온 놈이라는 것 정도는 알고 있었지만, 면구 제작법까지 익혔을 줄은 몰랐다.
268|
269|‘생각보다 쓸모가 많은 놈인데?’
270|
271|낭인 생활을 하며 터득한 여러 가지 경험도 앞으로의 길에 있어 큰 도움이 될 것이 분명하다.
272|
273|내심 송일섬에 대해 감탄하던 나는 문득 드는 생각에 눈을 크게 떴다.
274|
275|“잠깐. 그런데 왜 내 건 없어?”
276|
277|면구가 있었다면 언제 터질지 모르는 시한 똥폭탄을 옆에 두고 짐처럼 실려 갈 이유가 없는 것 아닌가.
278|
279|억울함을 성토하는 내 모습에 송일섬이 혀를 찼다.
280|
281|“사람마다 이목구비가 다르니 틀을 잡는 데에만 며칠이 걸리는 것이 면구다. 그런데 어떻게 그 촉박한 시간 동안 네놈 것까지 만들란 말이냐? 오히려 어색한 면구를 착용하면 역효과만 날 뿐이야. 정 억울하면 역용술(易容術)을 익혔어야지.”
282|
283|볼일을 마치고 세상 시원한 표정으로 풀숲을 빠져나온 혁무진이 끼어들었다.
284|
285|“그럼 주 소저는요? 며칠씩 걸린다면서요.”
286|
287|“소국주의 면구는…….”
288|
289|말꼬리를 흐린 송일섬이 문득 미간을 찌푸렸다.
290|
291|“쓸데없는 이야기로군. 닥치고 도로 볏짚 속에 파묻혀라. 면전에서 똥 냄새 풍기지 말고.”
292|
293|“지도 똥 싸는 주제에 되게 뭐라고 하네…….”
294|
295|궁시렁거리며 볏짚 속으로 기어들어 가는 혁무진의 모습을 노려본 송일섬이 내게 물었다.
296|
297|“베도 되나?”
298|
299|“안 돼.”
300|
301|단호하게 대답한 내가 주화란을 향해 물었다.
302|

“You’re on your sixth.”

[P65]
“…”

[P66]
“Let’s drink.”

[P67]

[P68]
*I wonder where he is down there.*

[P69]
*Heartless brat. You could’ve at least shown your face once before leaving.*

[P70]
The words in his heart scattered on a breeze that came from somewhere.

[P71]
* * *

[P72]
Clip-clop. Clip-clop.

[P73]
The old horse walked slowly, and the straw packed around my entire body was cold and prickly. Outside the carriage, the voices of hawkers and passersby gradually faded.

[P74]
*Did we make it out?*

[P75]
The thought had barely crossed my mind when someone whispered in my ear.

[P76]
“Captain. I need to take a shit.”

[P77]
“…”

[P78]
*Hyuk Mujin, you insane bastard. Even here?*

[P79]
We had to move as little as possible, so I couldn’t even beat him into submission. I kept my voice low as I snapped, “You lunatic. I told you to go before we left.”

[P80]
“I’m nervous. That’s why. I’m nervous.”

[P81]
“Then hold it, you son of a bitch.”

[P82]
“Why are you swearing at me? I can’t say a thing around you.”

[P83]
“How am I supposed to *not* swear? What are we going to do about the smell if you shit in here?”

[P84]
Even a fart under the same blanket would make me swear. I refused to suffer anything worse while we were buried together in straw.

[P85]
“I’ve been thinking about that. If I just went, wouldn’t the smell make it easier to get through inspection?”

[P86]
“Die. Please, just die.”

[P87]
“I’m sorry. I’ve held it as long as I can, but I don’t think I can hold it anymore. This might be the end for me.”

[P88]
“Hey, Mujin. Wait. Just wait a second.”

[P89]
“I’ll accept my punishment later.”

[P90]
*No! You bastard!*

[P91]
I was so terrified I was about to spring up, disguise be damned, when—

[P92]
“We’ve passed through the center of Luoyang. We’re on an empty mountain road now, so you can come out for a moment.”

[P93]
“Hah!”

[P94]
“Phew!”

[P95]
*Rustle!*

[P96]
Hyuk Mujin burst through the straw and sprinted toward the bushes. Saved at the edge of a cliff, I bowed repeatedly to my savior.

[P97]
“Thank you. I’ll be a good person. Thank you so much.”

[P98]
“The inspection must have taken a while for Young Hero Hyuk to be that desperate. I’m glad we weren’t too late.”

[P99]
The voice was familiar. The smiling woman’s face was not.

[P100]
In the moonlight spilling between the high branches, the freckles across her cheeks and her dry, rough skin stood out.

[P101]
*No matter how many times I look, it’s amazing.*

[P102]
Her features and a few small details had changed, yet the whole impression she gave was different.

[P103]
Ju Hwaran noticed me staring and touched her face. “Ah, I have changed a little, haven’t I?”

[P104]
“Yes. But your eyes are still the same.”

[P105]
A smile flickered in her beautiful dark-blue eyes.

[P106]
“A disguise mask can’t do anything about those. And without Captain Song, I couldn’t have found a mask this good on such short notice.”

[P107]
Song Ilseom, sitting on the driver’s bench, added flatly, “It was nothing. Just a little trick I learned to survive.”

[P108]
“That’s impressive for a little trick.”

[P109]
“I assume that’s empty praise, but I’ll thank you for it.”

[P110]
*That bastard has to take everything the wrong way. I meant it.*

[P111]
Song Ilseom had made the mask that turned Ju Hwaran into someone else entirely. I knew he’d started at the bottom and been through all kinds of hardship, but I hadn’t expected him to know how to make disguise masks.

[P112]
*He’s more useful than I thought.*

[P113]
The things he’d learned as a wandering martial artist would surely help us on the road ahead. I was admiring him in spite of myself when a thought made my eyes widen.

[P114]
“Wait. Why don’t I have one?”

[P115]
If I had a disguise mask, I wouldn’t have needed to ride like a piece of luggage beside a shit bomb that might go off at any moment.

[P116]
Song Ilseom clicked his tongue at my protest. “Everyone’s features are different. Just making the mold for a disguise mask takes days. How was I supposed to make yours in the time we had? A poorly fitted mask would only draw more attention. If you’re so upset, you should have learned a disguise technique.”

[P117]
Hyuk Mujin emerged from the bushes looking thoroughly relieved and joined in.

[P118]
“Then what about Young Lady Ju? You said it takes days.”

[P119]
“The Young Bureau Head’s mask…”

[P120]
Song Ilseom trailed off, then frowned. “What a pointless question. Shut up and get back under the straw. And keep that shit smell out of my face.”

[P121]
“You shit too. What are you getting on my case for…?”

[P122]
Song Ilseom glared as Hyuk Mujin grumbled his way back into the straw, then turned to me.

[P123]
“Can I cut him?”

[P124]
“No.”

[P125]
I turned to Ju Hwaran. “The others must be out by now, right?”

[P126]
She knew whom I meant and gave a small nod. “Probably. They went through the West Gate, where inspections are the weakest. They should have left Luoyang ahead of us.”

[P127]
Taishan’s size worried me, but Ju Hwaran had planned too carefully to overlook it. Besides, we had the Alliance Leader’s Hall and the Hidden Shadow Pavilion behind us. I could afford to relax.

[P128]
*Rustle.*

[P129]
Hyuk Mujin poked his head out of the straw. “Are we going straight to Mount Daebyeol, then?”

[P130]
“Of course. We’ll change horses once along the way, but there shouldn’t be any trouble before that.”

[P131]
Ju Hwaran continued without pause. “If we keep moving, two shichen. With thorough inspections, it could take three. Once we meet the other two at Mount Daebyeol…”

[P132]
“We leave Henan immediately. Correct?”

[P133]
She smiled and nodded. “Just as you said, Pavilion Master.”

[P134]
“…Pavilion Master?”

[P135]
“Why? Isn’t that the right title?”

[P136]
Technically, it was. It just felt like a set of clothes that didn’t fit. I smacked my lips and nodded.

[P137]
“Well, never mind that. We shouldn’t have any problems before Mount Daebyeol, then?”

[P138]
“Not at all. You could have a good long sleep and wake up before we arrive.”

[P139]
Henan was the Murim Alliance’s base. An enemy attack here was all but impossible. Still, I let out a quiet laugh, neither agreeing nor disagreeing.

[P140]
“What is it?”

[P141]
“Nothing.”

[P142]
How could I put it? I thought for a moment before going on.

[P143]
“It just feels strange to think I’ll be dreaming again after so long.”

[P144]
“Dreaming?”

[P145]
“Yes. I dream sometimes. So deeply I wouldn’t notice if someone carried me away.”

[P146]
Ju Hwaran looked puzzled. Song Ilseom frowned as if I were talking nonsense. Leaving them to it, I burrowed deep into the straw piled in the carriage.

[P147]
*Two shichen to Mount Daebyeol if we’re quick. That’s plenty of time.*

[P148]
It was time to have the dream I’d put off for so long.

[P149]
*Logout.*

[P150]
*Ding.*

[P151]
With the clear chime of a bell, my alert consciousness slowly began to sink.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
